lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The 4-2 victory over the Islanders stopped the bleeding, but it did not erase the bruise. Toronto is 9-14, 13th in the Eastern Conference with 21 points - hardly the profile of a club entitled to comfort - and now carries only a one-game winning streak into Boston. The latest storm centers on William Nylander: he has been dropped to the second power-play unit, and openly said he didn't agree with the decision. Jim Hiller calls it balance, arguing Nylander can become the focal point of the second group; Nylander sees the move through the lens of his costly Columbus turnover. Either way, a scorer who has gone eight games without a goal has been handed a challenge, not a compliment. At 1 p.m. ET against the Bruins, watch whether Nylander answers with the puck - and whether this fragile Toronto revival can survive a real test.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The offseason has produced a decision, not a detour. Toronto signed Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira to a five-year, $80 million contract, filling a rotation need while making the next priority unmistakable: bats. The Blue Jays' finished season sits at -2.0 points, but that number belongs in the rearview mirror; the argument now is whether this roster can manufacture enough offense to matter when the games count again. Seiya Suzuki looms as the cleanest answer on a market short on risk-free choices, though competition and a price reportedly north of $120 million will test Toronto's conviction. Taira's six-pitch mix gives the club intriguing rotation depth, but pitching alone will not repair an attack that needs more authority in the outfield and middle order. Watch the next move: Toronto's pursuit of Suzuki - or its pivot to another impact bat - will define whether Taira becomes a foundation piece or merely an expensive patch.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: A three-day breather did not erase the sting of a season that keeps asking Toronto to prove it belongs. The Raptors' 116-111 loss to Milwaukee on Monday left them 6-11, fourth in the Atlantic and 8 games behind, with a one-game skid hanging over a club still searching for steadiness under the weight of expectations. The injuries make that search harder: Kawhi Leonard remains out with left-knee swelling, R.J. Barrett is sidelined by a hamstring strain, and Nate Bittle is unavailable with a foot injury. Scottie Barnes now carries the visible burden, not as a savior but as the player who must organize a shorthanded attack and supply its edge. This is no routine November appointment - the NBA Cup creates genuine urgency. Friday's 7:30 p.m. meeting with Brooklyn is Toronto's chance to reset, stay alive in the Cup race and turn a rare break into something useful.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: Two wins have steadied Washington's season, but they have not erased its margin for error. The Commanders are 4-5-1, sitting second in the NFC East and two games back, after edging Cincinnati 22-20 on Nov. 23. The freshest jolt is Brandon Aiyuk's arrival on the practice squad - a sensible swing on a proven receiver, though two years away from NFL action makes instant rescue fantasy. Washington needs its existing playmakers to keep carrying the load, not wait for a name to save the offense. The timing is favorable: Carson Beck has missed two straight Cardinals practices with back spasms, leaving Arizona preparing for Josh Johnson if Beck cannot go. Still, road games punish sloppy confidence. Sunday's 4:25 p.m. visit to Arizona is the next test: extend the winning streak, or prove these Commanders are merely treading water.

article.title: Nylander Moves to Leafs Second Power Play
paragraphs: The Leafs visit the Bruins at 1:00 PM ET on TSN, with Anthony Stolarz starting against Jeremy Swayman. William Nylander is moving to the second power-play unit, while Kirill Marchenko returns to the top group. Nylander said he did not agree with the decision, and Toronto will also be without injured forward Roslovic. The Leafs enter at 9-14, 13th in the Eastern Conference.

The Blue Jays are looking ahead to their regular-season opener at the Yankees on Thursday, March 25, at 1:35 PM ET. Toronto is narrowing its offseason focus as more relievers leave the market. The Raptors host the Nets at 7:30 PM ET, with Leonard, Bittle and Barrett out and Martin day-to-day. Toronto is 6-11. The Commanders visit the Cardinals on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on Fox, carrying a 4-5-1 record and second place in the NFC East. Carson Beck remains out of Arizona practice.
